structured_output.summary:
The loop has stalled at the E116 tip: 4.26 s, population mean 0.7521, and about a 27% chance of passing the 3-seed gate on any one attempt. Every lever tried since E125 (E125–E134) either cost accuracy at or above the measured yardstick or did nothing. The tree hasn't caught up with this. H8, H8.3.1, H2.11.7, H2.20.2, H12.3.1 and H2.18/H2.18.4 are still marked open even though E132, E134, E133, E131 and E130 contradict them. H2's list of "live levers" is almost entirely closed, and H2.23's combination plan now has nothing left to combine.

The biggest methodological gap is resolution. Nearly every zero-time knob was closed on 3-seed runs before the 100-seed instrument existed (E113). A 3-seed run has a two-arm SE of about 0.2 pp, while the large-seed instrument has about 0.035 pp. The knobs closed this way include label smoothing (E037), Muon momentum (E030), warmup (E051/E059), the Muon floor (E057) and the whitening-bias window (E061). The most informative recent results are large drops when augmentation or data coverage is increased or reduced: E131 translate 4 cost −0.56 pp and E124 duplicated images cost −0.82 pp. Even so, augmentation was closed after testing only one direction. Weaker augmentation and lower LS have never been measured at large seed.

The current Lvl1 hypotheses don't explain one consistent pattern. Every decrement costs accuracy (early updates in E134, 16 px samples in E132, late updates in E126, freeze depth and point, network depth), while the one increment tested at 100 seeds (E121, more early updates) gained nothing. H8 says the early phase has a threshold and H11 says late training is what binds; neither predicts this. The simpler reading is that the greedy search has put the recipe on a frontier where every schedule or batch trade costs about the same. If so, more trims won't help. Progress needs either margin from re-screening zero-time knobs at large seed, or a structural change, such as a byte-oriented redesign of the early high-resolution stage.

Bookkeeping issues: some baselines don't match the arms they're compared against (E124 and E131 are built on E100 but compared with E116). The E133 rejection rests on a difference of about 1.3 SE from the floor. H4.9's limit of 3 scored attempts is being bypassed by counting tip reruns as scored rows.

critiques.issue: H8 (open, 0.40) made two predictions: early bs 2048 with step-fixed warmup would be null, and trimming 16 px would cost well under 0.05 pp per 1%. Both are refuted at 100 seeds. E134 cost −0.30 pp, about 0.2 pp per 1%. E132 cost −0.17 pp, about 0.055–0.075 pp per 1%. H8.3.1 still lists E132- under status 'open'. The claim that the threshold applies to update count and not to samples also fails, because removing samples (E132) hurt too.
critiques.suggestion: Mark H8.3.1 refuted and H2.11.7 refuted. Rewrite H8 as an asymmetric response: adding early updates or samples does nothing (E121, E114), removing them costs at or above the yardstick (E132, E134, E032, E041, E043). Since that is a description and not a mechanism, either retire H8 or merge it into a single 'tuned frontier' Lvl1 (see the H2 critique).

critiques.target: H2 (Lvl1 statement, live-lever list) and H2.23 / H2.23.1
critiques.issue: Most of H2's 'Live levers' are now dead. Earlier freeze 75–80% is closed by E133 (marginal ~0.06 pp per 1%). 3/3/2 is closed by E130 (−0.48 pp, 0.08 per 1%). Early bs 2048 is closed by E134 and the 16 px trim by E132. H2.23.1 needs several levers measured at ≤0.045 pp per 1%, but the only unbanked one left is 2/3/3 at 0.041. Funded by re-spending time at 32 px, it nets about −0.6%, which is inside error. Re-spend also has to use the upward arm of E128 (+0.24 pp for +5.5%, about 0.044 per 1%), not the 0.05 average. On that basis 2/3/3 roughly breaks even, and depth may not combine additively with the 32 px epoch slope.
critiques.suggestion: Prune the live list to what is actually untested: FreezeOut BN-eval (H2.20.6), group-3 width 512, group-1 width or earlier downsampling, lookahead removal and Muon-C. Mark H2.18 and H2.18.4 refuted, since E130 was that exact run. Put H2.23.1 on hold until at least two levers are measured below 0.04 pp per 1%. Use 0.044 as the funding rate and 0.054 as the pure-cut rate.

critiques.target: H6 / H7.1 / H12 closures made before E113 (E030, E034, E037, E051, E057, E059, E061, E009)
critiques.issue: The tree treats scalar knobs as exhausted, but most were closed on single 3-seed runs. Their two-arm SE is about 0.2 pp, so effects up to roughly ±0.3 pp were never excluded. The loop now needs about 0.1 pp of margin, and its instrument can resolve 0.07 pp at 2 SE. LS under Muon (E037: 0.7550 vs ~0.7554) and Muon momentum 0.5 (E030) are each one 3-seed sample against a tip that was itself a high draw.
critiques.suggestion: Run a large-seed re-screen batch. Each arm is untimed, 100 seeds, compared against the pooled E116 baseline: LS 0.2 and 0.25; Muon momentum 0.5 and 0.7; the 64x BN-bias SGD multiplier at 32x and 96x; BN momentum. A +0.1 pp gain buys about 2% time through a 32 px trim at 0.054 pp per 1%.

critiques.target: H12 / H12.3.1 (augmentation closed after one direction)
critiques.issue: E131 (translate 4, −0.56 pp at 100 seeds), E124 (−0.82 pp) and E008 (SGD jitter) all show that more augmentation or less coverage hurts strongly. With a steep response like that, the optimum may sit below translate 2. The tree closed augmentation strength without testing the weaker direction. H12.3.1 is also still marked 'open' even though E131- is recorded.
critiques.suggestion: Mark H12.3.1 refuted, then open its mirror. In the 28/32 px phases, test translate 1 and translate 0 (flip kept), and separately no flip in the last 32 px epoch, each at 100 seeds. This is zero-time and is the best-motivated untested accuracy source, given that the tip is under-trained (~1 pp per 32 px epoch).

critiques.target: E132 / E134 design (confounds behind the H8 refutation)
critiques.issue: E132 rescaled LR warmup/decay, the floor-hold and the renorm cadence to the shorter total. That shrinks the LR schedule seen by every later phase, not just the 16 px exposure. E134 kept the whitening-bias detach indexed by samples, so the 64x-LR bias got about 25% fewer update steps (E093 shows that bias is fragile). It also applied the kilostep SGD rescale and lengthened warmup in sample terms. Neither result is a clean test of the mechanism it is used to reject.
critiques.suggestion: If H8 is going to be stated as a mechanism, run the clean versions. For E132: drop the first 0.5 epoch but keep the absolute post-16-px schedule. For E134: keep the whitening-bias step count fixed and skip the SGD rescale. Otherwise state H8 descriptively and don't build on its mechanism.

critiques.issue: H11 says late fresh samples and updates bind while marginal low-res steps add nothing. The decrement results don't single out late training. Early update removal (E134, −0.30) and early sample removal (E132, −0.17) cost as much as or more than late removal (E126, −0.18; E128, −0.25 per 0.25 epoch). The only increment tested at 100 seeds (E121, early) was null, and no late increment has been tested at large seed. The evidence is equally consistent with 'every decrement hurts, increments saturate', which isn't late-specific. E126 also confounds EMA-window samples, SGD rescale and Muon path length.
critiques.suggestion: Run H11.2.2 (the E126 confound ablation) before H2.11.5. Also add a late increment at 100 seeds (bs 768 in the last 32 px epoch, as in H2.11.5). Without it, the claim that late updates are worth more than early ones rests only on decrements, which hurt everywhere.

critiques.issue: H2.11 says the results contradict gradient-noise-scale theory. Read through critical batch size, they partly fit it: early, B_crit sits between 1536 and 2048 (E121 null, E134 −0.30); late, the 32 px phase prefers 1024 (E126). The remaining puzzle is why the late critical batch looks smaller, and E126's confounds (window, SGD rescale) may be what produces it. Separately, the E121 notebook claim that E084's late gain was 'likely noise' is contradicted by E126, which reverses E084 and confirms it at large seed.
critiques.suggestion: Restate H2.11 in critical-batch terms with a falsifiable prediction for each phase. Correct the E121 note: E084's direction is confirmed by E126.

critiques.issue: E133's population mean (0.75106 over 200 trajectories, SE ~0.018 pp) misses the 0.7513 floor by 0.024 pp, about 1.3 SE. The floor was itself set from first principles (3 sd of the 40-seed mean), and 0.75106 still gives P(official < 0.75) ≈ 0.5%. So E133's rejection, with a passing scored row at 4.190 s (−1.7%), turns on a policy constant and noise. Separately, H4.9's '≤3 scored attempts' is being bypassed: E116 code has 7 scored rows because tip reruns were attached as the scored row of other experiments. That gives a pass chance of about 1−0.73^7 ≈ 89% instead of the intended ~61%.
critiques.suggestion: Write down whether the floor is a hard rule or a soft one, and report E133 as a policy rejection, not an accuracy refutation. Count every scored rerun of the same code toward the attempt budget, or drop the budget explicitly. Make sure submissions/arena actually holds E116 code: results.tsv marks E133 as feasible/improved, so a 'best feasible row' selection could pick it.

critiques.target: H4.2.4 provenance / baseline mismatches in E124 and E131
critiques.issue: E124 and E131 were built on E100 code, which has no freeze, but compared against the E116 baseline 'on the same seeds'. E100 is about +0.09 pp above E116, so the reported −0.82 and −0.56 pp understate the effects (true deltas ≈ −0.91 and −0.65). E123's provenance is still unresolved. H4.2.4 has been open for dozens of experiments.
critiques.suggestion: Recompute every large-seed delta against the baseline of its actual base code, and log the source hash plus diff as a hard precondition. This won't flip the E124/E131 verdicts, but the loop is now making 0.05 pp decisions, where a 0.09 pp offset matters.

critiques.target: H13 / H9.2.2 / H9.2.3 (tip components adopted on ≤1.5 SE)
critiques.issue: Several components still in the tip rest on one run or 8 seeds: head on Muon (E044, one run), head lr 0.5x, Muon x1.25 at 32 px (null at population level per E113), lookahead (E092, 8 seeds) and the final EMA (E079, 8 seeds). These removal ablations are the cheapest zero-time margin sources left, and the instrument was never applied to them.
critiques.suggestion: Make H13.1.1, H9.2.2 and H9.2.3 the next batch. Each is untimed, 100 seeds, and needs no recompile. A null lookahead removal also banks about 0.4% time.

critiques.issue: Every Muon matrix here has out < in·9; the head [100, 576] also has out < in. For a full-row-rank semi-orthogonal update UVᵀ, every row already has unit norm. NorMuon's row normalization would therefore only correct NS imprecision, and E033 showed that better orthogonalization (NS 4) gained nothing.
critiques.suggestion: Retire H7.5 on this argument without a run.

critiques.issue: The proposed mechanism is better-conditioned conv updates. E033 (NS 4: 83% of singular values in band vs 56%, +0 pp) is direct local evidence that conditioning quality doesn't bind at this budget. The cost is also about 3.7x the NS FLOPs on a per-step cost already measured at ~1.7–2 ms per step.
critiques.suggestion: Lower the prior. If it runs at all, require the untimed overhead measurement first, and set the accuracy bar at ≥0.15 pp at 100 seeds, which it already has.

critiques.issue: A FLOP + byte cost model only has value if it points to a lever. After E130–E134, the only byte lever with headroom is redesigning the 31×31 stage, and H2.21.4 (earlier pool in group 1) is gated behind this model. The model and its reconciliation runs (H2.21.3, H2.22.1) can't produce a speedup by themselves.
critiques.suggestion: Skip ahead: profile untimed a stem/group-1 variant that downsamples earlier (pool after conv1, or a stride-2 stem) along with group-1 width 96. Score at 100 seeds only if the projected saving is ≥8%. Use the cost model only to explain the result afterwards.

critiques.target: E003 / H2.2 (activation closed under SGD only)
critiques.issue: GELU→SiLU (−2.2% time, −0.61 pp) is a single 3-seed SGD run from before the Muon regime, the 0.05 pp per 1% yardstick, and the large-seed instrument. Under Muon the accuracy cost of an activation change has never been measured. At the yardstick, −2.2% time only needs ≤0.11 pp loss to break even.
critiques.suggestion: Low priority, but cheap: profile SiLU (and ReLU) on the tip for time, and if the saving is still ≥2%, run 100 seeds.

critiques.issue: H2.10 still says 'Low-res trims have never been measured at large seed', but E132 has since measured one. H2.1's claim that 16 px works 'for the first ~2 epochs' rests on E026 and E029/E040/E046, which were 3-seed runs against references that were often lucky draws. E041's closure of the 20 px bridge (−0.38 pp vs E035's high draw of 0.7572) is a single 3-seed comparison.
critiques.suggestion: Update H2.10 with E132. If a structural change is ever made to the early stage, re-measure the 20 px bridge at 100 seeds before treating it as closed.

critiques.target: Missing Lvl1: why every local trade lands at ~0.05 pp per 1%
critiques.issue: The large-seed results line up suspiciously well. The 32 px trim costs 0.054 per 1%, the 16 px trim 0.055–0.075, the group-2 freeze 0.055, the 85→80% freeze 0.06, 2/3/3 0.04, and 3/3/2 0.08.
